# DSH Context OS
English | 简体中文

> **ReAct is all you need.**
> **Everything is a context connector.**
**Compose each agent run from complete, replaceable resource services.**
DSH Context OS is a plugin for DeepSeek Harness. Choose the environment, code, conversation history,
documents and other services for this run. Each service supplies context and handles the interactio
ns it owns. The framework composes their contributions around the agent loop.
ReAct combines reasoning and acting. Our slogan expresses an architectural thesis: keep that loop ge
neral, and make its connection to the world composable.
**Status:** experimental `0.2.0`. The composition runtime and drag-and-drop Web UI work today. The c
omplete mode uses the included launcher with a pinned DSH build. Service-wide resource auditing and
agent-assisted configuration are next steps. See current scope.
## Start with the run
Many agent products organize everything around a workspace, a persistent session, a skill directory
or a fixed set of tools. Those are useful product choices. They also become architectural assumption
s: where files live, how history is restored, which instructions are loaded, and how outside service
live, how history is restored, which instructions are loaded, and how outside services can respond.
We choose a smaller foundation: **an agent loop running with a particular context composition**.
For a given model and runtime configuration, the context assembled for the model—and the information
and capabilities it can reach—are central product variables. Context includes instructions, history
, task input, capability descriptions and observations returned from the world. Improving it means s
upplying the right information at the right time, with access to the right resources.
This leads to two responsibilities:

- **The framework defines how context is composed and how events are delivered.**
- **Service provid
ers decide what to contribute, when to contribute it, and how their resources work.**
A document platform can offer guidance, search, editing, permissions and persistence together. An in
put method, a log stream or a history recommender can participate through the same boundary. Skill a
nd MCP remain useful integration formats; they do not define the framework's service model.
This project develops the proposal in Context assembly and feedback as the framework boundary.
## Three layers, one feedback loop
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**One connector owns one complete service.** Its instructions, callable capabilities, execution feed
back, persistence and cleanup stay together. A sandbox service can contribute system guidance and fi
le/shell capabilities through the same protocol as a document service contributes editing guidance a
nd document operations.
The framework owns contribution identity, ordering, validation and assembly. DSH owns the native loo
p. Construction and service dependencies use DSH/Cordis; a repository provider that needs an executi
on provider uses those existing dependency mechanisms.
A run follows the same path for every service:
1. Selected connectors initialize and contribute instructions, capabilities and, where applicable, c

oherent history.
2. Before each model step, the framework combines their current contributions into

the next input.
3. The model requests an operation. The framework routes it to the connector that ow

ns it.
4. That service operates on its resources and returns an answer, possibly with updated contex

t for a later step.
5. Records and settlement events return to the services for persistence and clea
nup. They can also contribute context for subsequent work.
The same boundary supports both initial assembly and ongoing feedback. Loading knowledge on demand,
receiving a new log entry and returning a tool result all fit into it.
## Why this changes what products can do
### Replace the execution environment as a complete service
Moving a coding agent from a host machine to a sandbox is difficult when file reads, file writes, di
rectory inspection, environment checks, shell execution and workspace instructions are spread across
the agent's implementation. Redirecting commands alone can leave filesystem checks or environment d
escriptions pointing at the original host.
With Context OS, an execution provider owns this whole resource boundary:
| Responsibility | What the environment connector supplies |
| Describe the environment | System or user context explaining paths, available software and operati

ng constraints |
| Inspect and change resources | Callable descriptions and implementations for its

file, directory and command operations |
| Return observations | Results and context updates from th

e environment actually used |
| Manage the lifecycle | Provisioning or attachment, provider-side aut
horization, cancellation handling and release |
Switching from a local provider to a sandbox provider changes the selected service. The core still c
omposes instructions and routes owned requests. Compatible repository and document services keep the
ir contracts; dependencies remain explicit.
**The migration becomes an implementation of the environment service contract, with a smaller change
surface and reusable tests.** The provider still implements the actual isolation, resource access a
nd lifecycle. Merely describing a sandbox in a prompt does not create one.
### Continue a conversation across machines
When persistence and resume logic are inseparable from a coding agent, continuing elsewhere can requ
ire moving local session files, reproducing directory layouts and adapting the agent's recovery path
re moving local session files, reproducing directory layouts and adapting the agent's recovery path.
Here, selected history is one source of context. A session provider loads it, converts it to the acc
epted representation, receives new records and persists the result. Its backend can be local storage
or a remote service.
